title: What do positive five and negative eight add up to?
description: Five positive tokens and eight negative tokens are put side by side. Five zero pairs are matched and taken away, and the tokens left give the sum. Keeko thinks the sign comes from the number written first.
teaching_notes: One idea: cancel zero pairs, and the sign of the tokens left is the sign of the sum. Watch for students who keep the sign of the first number instead of looking at which tokens are left.

video_script.why: The child adds a positive and a negative number with tokens and sees that the tokens left decide the sign of the sum.
video_script.substitution: Match each positive token with a negative token, take away the zero pairs, and read the sum from the tokens left.
video_script.anchor: five positive tokens and eight negative tokens on the board
video_script.wrong_move: keeps the sign of the number written first and ignores which tokens are left over
video_script.payoff_line: Positive five plus negative eight leaves negative three.
maths_rules: +5 means 5 positive tokens; −8 means 8 negative tokens: (+5) + (−8)
1 positive and 1 negative token make a zero pair: (+1) + (−1) = 0
5 positive tokens match 5 negative tokens, giving 5 zero pairs
slip: the sign of the first number (+5) is not the sign of the sum
video_script.design: One idea: take away the zero pairs and read the sum, with its sign, from the tokens left. Positive tokens are green and negative tokens are red as in the book. Keeko's doubt is that the first number gives the sign.
